run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The recommendation service became unreachable for its callers in the last ~2 minutes of the sampled window. Blackbox probe_success for recommendation.astronomy-shop:8080 dropped from 1 (13:42) to 0 (13:43, 13:44) while the other 15 blackbox targets stayed at 1, and frontend client spans for oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations fail with gRPC status 14 and the exact message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ETIMEDOUT 10.96.63.204:8080', so GET /api/recommendations returns HTTP 500 (frontend-proxy/load-generator observe 504). The recommendation pod itself is Running and Ready with 0 restarts and logged 'Recommendation service started, listening on port 8080' at 13:42:26, but its replacement pods never logged a received request (newest 'Receive ListRecommendations' line anywhere is 13:42:15.772 from the previous pod), so packets are being dropped before reaching the application rather than the application erroring. Service/Endpoints and the pod IP agree (10.244.234.168:8080), other pods on the same node (product-catalog, accounting) keep passing probes and receiving traffic, and the blackbox prober runs on sregym-control-plane, so neither a Service misconfiguration nor a node-wide outage explains it. The only change observed on recommendation immediately before traffic stopped is that Deployment recommendation (revision 3) was rolled twice: at 13:41:44 a new ReplicaSet carrying nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=sregym-worker, and at 13:42:23 another rollout (kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt) replacing the last pod that was still serving. The object that actually applies the packet drop is not readable from the available evidence (no NetworkPolicy objects exist in the namespace; Calico policy resources and change history are not readable), so the causal link to the Deployment change is stated as a hypothesis, not a proven fact.

claims.text: Prometheus shows alert ServiceEndpointDown firing for instance recommendation.astronomy-shop:8080 in namespace astronomy-shop (deployment=recommendation, job=blackbox-astronomy-shop, severity critical, activeAt 2026-11-21T13:42:49Z) and HighRequestErrorRate pending for GET /api/recommendations?productIds=9SIQT8TOJO with value 0.97 at 13:43:26Z.

Blackbox probes: probe_success for instance recommendation.astronomy-shop:8080 was 1 at 13:42:00Z, then 0 at 13:43:00Z and 0 at 13:44:00Z, while all 15 other blackbox-astronomy-shop instances (ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, flagd, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, kafka, payment, product-catalog, product-reviews, quote, shipping) reported 1 at 13:43:00Z and 13:44:00Z.

Frontend client spans oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations carry rpc.grpc.status_code=14, error=true and grpc.error_message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ETIMEDOUT 10.96.63.204:8080 (2026-11-21T13:44:38.326Z)' for requests starting 13:43:05Z through 13:44:07Z, and the parent GET /api/recommendations spans on service frontend return http.status_code=500.

The same failing requests carry frontend-proxy GET spans with http.status_code=504 and load-generator GET spans with http.status_code=504 (error=true), so the user-visible symptom is a gateway timeout/500 on the recommendation page path.

Pod recommendation-77d86ff87-4skxz on node sregym-worker has podIP 10.244.234.168, phase Running, condition Ready=True since 13:42:25Z, container state running with restartCount 0 and lastState empty.
The recommendation container has no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe defined, so Ready=True on this pod reflects container start, not a successful serving check.
Pod recommendation-77d86ff87-4skxz logs contain only the startup lines, including '2026-11-21 13:42:26,329 ... Recommendation service started, listening on port 8080', and no request-handling lines.

The newest 'Receive ListRecommendations' log line from any recommendation-* pod in 13:41:00Z-13:44:14Z is 2026-11-21T13:42:15.772271829Z from pod recommendation-5bb649dccb-2d524; the replacement pods recommendation-6b9dd6f6fc-cdkwh (started listening 13:41:47) and recommendation-77d86ff87-4skxz (started listening 13:42:26) produced no such line.

Service recommendation selects opentelemetry.io/name=recommendation and maps port 8080 to targetPort 8080, and its Endpoints subset lists address 10.244.234.168 with targetRef Pod recommendation-77d86ff87-4skxz, i.e. the endpoint matches the pod IP; there is no selector/port/IP mismatch.

Deployment recommendation is at metadata revision 3 with nodeSelector {kubernetes.io/hostname: sregym-worker}; of the 23 deployments in astronomy-shop only recommendation and frontend carry a nodeSelector (all other 21 have none).

ReplicaSet templates for recommendation differ only in scheduling/rollout metadata: recommendation-5bb649dccb has no nodeSelector, recommendation-6b9dd6f6fc adds nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=sregym-worker, and recommendation-77d86ff87 adds nodeSelector plus pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-21T13:42:23Z; all three use image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-recommendation.

Deployment recommendation events show 'Scaled up replica set recommendation-6b9dd6f6fc from 0 to 1' at 13:41:44Z, 'Scaled down replica set recommendation-5bb649dccb from 1 to 0' at 13:41:46Z, 'Scaled up replica set recommendation-77d86ff87 from 0 to 1' at 13:42:23Z and 'Scaled down replica set recommendation-6b9dd6f6fc from 1 to 0' at 13:42:25Z.

The blackbox exporter pod (prometheus-prometheus-blackbox-exporter-6cdc44b585-wpljz) runs on node sregym-control-plane with podIP 10.244.116.177, a different node from both the recommendation pod (sregym-worker) and the frontend pod (sregym-worker2).

Load-generator counters for the 10 minutes to 13:44:00Z: /api/recommendations?productIds=HQTGWGPNH4 3.14 failures of 4.19 requests, /api/recommendations?productIds=9SIQT8TOJO 2.00 of 2.10, /api/recommendations?productIds=1YMWWN1N4O 1.00 of 1.05, Aggregated 13.02 failures of 165.27 requests.

Checked and found healthy: all 27 astronomy-shop pods are Running with restartCount 0; 15 of 16 blackbox targets pass; product-catalog (also on sregym-worker, podIP 10.244.234.176) still has spans at 1.64/s at 13:44:00Z and its probe stayed 1, so cross-node connectivity to sregym-worker pods and the node itself are not broken.

Rejected as the cause: an application-level recommendation failure driven by the flagd flag 'recommendationCacheFailure'. That flag is present with defaultVariant 'off' (state ENABLED) in the flagd-config demo.flagd.json actually mounted in astronomy-shop, and the observed error is a TCP-level connect timeout before the service with no received request logged and no server-side error span, which an in-process cache failure would not produce.

Rejected as the cause: a recommendation Service/Endpoints misconfiguration (wrong selector, wrong targetPort or missing endpoint). The selector matches the pod labels, port 8080 maps to targetPort 8080, and the Endpoints address 10.244.234.168 equals the running pod's podIP.

Rejected as the cause: a node-wide failure on sregym-worker. Other pods on that node (product-catalog, accounting, email, flagd, image-provider, kafka, payment, postgresql, product-reviews, quote, shipping) kept passing the blackbox probe at 13:43:00Z and 13:44:00Z, and product-catalog kept serving spans.

Traffic destined for the recommendation pod is being dropped on its network path (blackhole / 100% loss) rather than refused by the application: clients get a TCP connect timeout to 10.96.63.204:8080, the replacement pod is running and listening but never logged a received request, and the failure follows the pod while other pods on the same node remain reachable.

The loss of reachability coincides with the two Deployment recommendation rollouts (13:41:44Z nodeSelector rollout, 13:42:23Z restartedAt rollout) that replaced the last pod observed serving requests (last 'Receive ListRecommendations' 13:42:15.772Z); the replacement pods never received a request. Causality is plausible from timing and object identity but is not proven, because no readable object shows the packet drop being applied.

Read the Calico datastore on the cluster for GlobalNetworkPolicy/NetworkPolicy objects selecting opentelemetry.io/name=recommendation, and check calico-node/chaos-agent logs on sregym-worker around 13:41-13:43Z, to identify the object that applies the drop.

Capture packet counters or tcpdump inside the recommendation pod netns and on sregym-worker for 10.244.234.168:8080 to confirm whether SYNs are dropped at ingress, and verify whether the same pod is reachable from a pod on its own node.
Add readiness/liveness probes to the recommendation container so a pod that is running but not serving is not reported Ready.

gaps: No readable object shows what applied the packet drop to the recommendation pod: a cluster-wide NetworkPolicy query returned zero objects at 13:45:44Z (empty result, not citable as fact), the pods list contains no chaos-mesh/network-chaos components, and Calico policy custom resources are not readable with the available kinds.

The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so who/what patched Deployment recommendation at 13:41:44Z (nodeSelector) and 13:42:23Z (kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt) cannot be established.
Whether the recommendation pod is reachable from pods on its own node (sregym-worker) or only blackholed cross-node cannot be determined from the available metrics, traces and logs.

Span-metric series for this namespace only start around 13:42:30Z (fresh stack start at 13:40:49Z-13:42:26Z) and frontend/recommendation ListRecommendations series read 0 at 13:44:00Z despite observed calls, so no pre-incident baseline exists and span-metric export lag is unknown; the request-stop conclusion rests on client error spans and container logs.

traces_search for service recommendation in 13:42:30Z-13:44:14Z and traces_search_by_tags for service checkout with error=true returned no data (empty query results are not proof of absence); recommendation-server and checkout-side behaviour in that interval is therefore unverified.

Load-generator also reports /api/checkout failures (1.05 of 6.28 requests in the 10 minutes to 13:44:00Z) that I did not tie to any observed error span or to the recommendation fault; this remains unexplained.

The exact HTTP response the blackbox prober received (timeout versus refused) is not in its logs (Loki query for the blackbox exporter returned no matching lines), so the drop-versus-reject distinction rests on the gRPC client error text.
next_steps: Inspect Calico GlobalNetworkPolicy/NetworkPolicy and any node-level fault-injection agent state on sregym-worker for rules targeting 10.244.234.168 or the recommendation pod labels.
Capture tcpdump/packet counters in the recommendation pod netns and on sregym-worker and on a peer node to confirm where the SYNs are dropped.

Once an external change record is available, confirm which actor patched Deployment recommendation (nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=sregym-worker, restartedAt 2026-11-21T13:42:23Z) and whether it also applied the network fault.
